author: philly leader
title: A.J. Brown calls for Eagles offense to improve ahead of Lions matchup
text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are preparing for their upcoming Sunday night game against the Detroit Lions, with wide receiver A.J. Brown emphasizing the need for offensive improvement despite the team’s 7-2 record, which currently leads the NFC.
Brown addressed reporters following Wednesday’s walk-through practice, reflecting on the team’s recent victory over Green Bay and his own return from a hamstring injury that kept him out of the previous week’s game against the Giants. He finished Monday’s game with two receptions for 13 yards, bringing his season totals to 31 catches for 408 yards and three touchdowns.
“If we’re really focusing on winning and doing our job, we can’t just keep slapping the Band-Aid over the defense doing their job and getting us out of trouble. At what point are we going to pick up our slack as an offense,” Brown said. “We have to adapt and we have to continue to get better and try to find new ways.”
He also discussed how opposing defenses have been covering him: “Yes, I dictate the cover. That’s every single week. If you look back on film, every single game, I’m getting clouded. There’s no surprise. When we play Detroit on Sunday night, they play a lot of man. I’m pretty sure they’re going to cloud.”
During Monday night’s win in Green Bay, Brown played a role in freeing up space for teammate DeVonta Smith’s 36-yard touchdown reception from quarterback Jalen Hurts—a play that secured the Eagles’ victory.
“Me freeing up the play for DeVonta, I don’t have a problem with that. I want to see my team win. I want to see the offense thriving, passing,” Brown said.
“We always go into it with a great game plan, trying to do certain things, and I understand how the game goes.”
Brown joined the Eagles in 2022 and set a franchise record by recording 155 receiving yards in his first game with the team—the most ever by an Eagle making their debut.
